theme: La familia y los amigos en detalle; los posesivos; describir el carácter de las personas — el hijo pródigo
storyThread: El hijo pródigo (Lucas 15:24). L1 = la familia en detalle (re-passes de unit-01 + los abuelos). L2 = los amigos y los vecinos: tío, tía, primo, prima, amigo, amiga, vecino, vecina. L3 = los posesivos en profundidad: mis, tus, sus, nuestra, nuestros. L4 = el carácter del padre y de los dos hermanos: generoso, egoísta, humilde, orgulloso, celoso, paciente.
grammarTargets: possessive adjectives AGREE with the THING owned, not the owner: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/nuestra/nuestros/nuestras — taught by note + gap-fill with the written noun (E6 precedent); no new possessive ids beyond the 5 new ones (mis, tus, sus, nuestra, nuestros)

the mi/tu/su paradigm exception (a1-u02) remains the ONLY hear-choose paradigm exception, now extended by mis/tus/sus under the SAME logic (U6-7) — the person IS the contrast when the noun is identical
ser + character adjective vs estar + state: es generoso (trait) vs está enojado (state) — taught by note + say, no new ids
family nouns are SINGULAR citation forms with plurals in say/reading only (moneda precedent); padres is say-text ONLY — a DIFFERENT word from padre (U6-6), never an option string
present tense ONLY — pretérito is A1-U7; the parable's past-tense narration is NOT reproduced in any authored line (the scripture passage is exempt per the standing ruling)
«¿De quién es?» pattern lives in say/sign — de and quién are already bound ids (phrase-vs-word, ¿Cuánto cuesta? precedent)
waveNotes: l1 (9) = 7 byte-identical re-passes (unit-01 family wave — the A1 depth re-pass, C8) + abuelo/abuela new; the GENDER PARADIGM PAIRS (padre/madre, hermano/hermana, hijo/hija, abuelo/abuela) never share a hear-choose set (U6-8) — the contrast is tested in gap-fill with the written noun (E6). l2 (8) = the extended family and friends, all new; every gender pair never shares a set (U6-8). l3 (12) = the possessives: 5 re-passes (mi a0-u01; tu/su/nuestro/mío a1-u02) + 7 new (mis, tus, sus, nuestra, nuestros, tuyo, suyo). The PARADIGM EXCEPTION holds: mi/tu/su may share a hear-choose set (a1-u02, unchanged) and mis/tus/sus + mío/tuyo/suyo join under the same logic (U6-7); mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, mío/mi, tuyo/tu, suyo/su and the nuestro/nuestra/nuestros series may NOT (U6-7). l4 (12) = the character of the parable's people: 2 re-passes (bueno a0-u01; corazón a1-u05, U5-4 DISCHARGED — new:false) + 10 new. The OPPOSITE PAIRS sit together on purpose (bueno/malo, humilde/orgulloso, generoso/egoísta, celoso/enojado). Waves AT the 12-per-page threshold (DEFECTS #18) — no pagination; wave 5 = adaptive replay from progress.misses (unchanged convention).

qna.grammar: A1 register per THEOLOGY-guide §3.1: PRESENT TENSE ONLY — pretérito is A1-U7 and the parable's past-tense narration is NOT reproduced in any authored line; the scripture passage is exempt (standing ruling). No subjunctive; affirmative familiar imperatives only (toca, señala). Every say is one idea and the target word is repeated in caption + sign. Possessive agreement is taught by note + say, never by minting new ids; character adjectives are masculine citation forms or gender-invariant forms — the -a/-os/-as forms are never ids (a0-u06 descriptorDecision, a1-u04 E6).
qna.csa: Owner plain-truth directive applied: nothing softened, nothing added. The parable's sin is named plainly — the son takes his share, leaves, and wastes it (egoísta, malo); the older brother is proud, jealous and angry (orgulloso, celoso, enojado) — and the father's mercy is the story's own point (generoso, paciente, amable). No line moralizes beyond the text, no invented detail, no dramatization; character words describe the parable's people, NEVER the learner, and no system scores a learner's character (INT-1 holds). Repentance and restoration are the verse's own words (Lucas 15:24) — taught plainly per theology guide §3.3, with the father's mercy as the story's own point, never a measurement device.
qna.formIdRule: ids are the exact form the learner hears and the string on the tile. Possessive adjectives are BARE forms with the noun phrase in say/sign (the ¿Cuánto cuesta? phrase-vs-word precedent) — «¿De quién es?» lives in say/sign because de and quién are already bound ids. Family nouns are SINGULAR citation forms with plurals in say/reading only (moneda precedent). Character adjectives are masculine citation forms or gender-invariant forms; agreement forms are never ids.
